svg.title: A reproducible Schelling-style local-movement simulation
svg.desc: Three panels show a random initial population, the population after one sweep, and the final state in a declared Schelling-style model. Local moves increase the average share of same-group neighbors even though no agent seeks aggregate segregation.
svg.text: LOCAL MOVES CAN CREATE AN AGGREGATE PATTERN
One seeded teaching run: agents move when their same-group share is below one-third.
18 × 14 bounded grid · 38 vacancies · 107 agents per group · Moore neighbours · minimum same-group share = 1/3
Each sweep shuffles occupied cells; an unsatisfied agent moves uniformly among currently satisfying vacancies.
Python random.Random · seed 20260830 · one executable teaching hypothesis, not evidence about a real neighbourhood
